solves: A list of sections with a title that the person opens and closes in place to see the content of each one, without leaving the screen. Open, the content pushes down what comes below and covers nothing. It holds the items, the rule between them and the opening rule: several at once, or one at a time.
use_when: The screen has several supporting sections and the person reads one or a few at a time: the details of a record, frequently asked questions, filters in a side panel, the steps of a setup.
Grouped, in the page body, for the details of a record or frequently asked questions.
Separated, when each section is an independent block, such as the steps of a setup; with the single expansion when one step leads to the next.
Flush, in a side panel or inside another container such as a card or a dialog, so two outlines do not add up.
Multiple expansion when the person compares sections; single when the sections are a step-by-step.
A start (icon, tile, avatar or image) to recognize the section at a glance, a tag for a short highlight and an end status for the progress.
do_not_use_when: For a single section: use nph-collapsible.
For sections of the same weight seen one at a time: use nph-tabs.
For content everybody needs to read: keep the essential open on the page.
To hide an error, a warning or a pending required field in a closed item: show the pending item in text, in the description or in the end status.
Inside another accordion: use sections with a title on the page.
For an action in the trigger: the trigger is the only child of the heading, so the action goes inside the content, with nph-button.

appearance.constraint: The Figma property `aparencia`. grouped is one container with the soft outline, the corner, the shadow and a divider between items. separated is a block per item with space between the blocks and no divider. flush has no container, no outline, no padding and no shadow, with the divider between items. A value outside the list draws nothing and emits console.error in development.

expansion.constraint: The Figma property `expansao`. multiple lets each item open and close alone. single closes the open item when another opens; the open item can also close, and all closed is allowed. The special cases of single are in the business rules. A value outside the list draws nothing and emits console.error in development.

size.constraint: The Figma property `tamanho`. It is the size of every item and never changes item by item: the accordion hands it to them. It changes the minimum height of the trigger and the size of the start media; in large the title takes text/label-lg. A value outside the list draws nothing and emits console.error in development.

heading-level.constraint: The level of the heading that holds each trigger, a whole number from 1 to 6. The level comes from the page, so the default is 3. A value outside the range draws nothing and emits console.error in development.

slot.constraint: The default slot holds the nph-accordion-item elements, one per section. Anything else is ignored and warned once in development. The minimum is one item.

item.label.constraint: The title of the section, already localized, and the first part of the accessible name of the trigger. It wraps. An item with no label is a mount: it draws nothing and says nothing, because the text may arrive after the first render.

item.description.constraint: A short line under the title, a few words, already localized. It is read inside the name of the button, after the tag and before the status. A long description goes in the content, which is the default slot of the item. There is no property to say that a description is long: a description that does not fit in a few words belongs in the content.

item.start.constraint: The Figma start set, one type per list. icon is a light nph-icon, tile is a light nph-icon on a tonal box, avatar is an nph-avatar and image is an nph-image 1:1. The four status values draw circle-check, triangle-exclamation, circle-xmark and clock. Empty draws none. The start media is decorative. A value outside the list draws nothing and emits console.error in development.

item.icon.constraint: The core name of the nph-icon of the icon and tile starts, in the light weight; gear and folder when empty. Ignored with another start, and warned once in development. A name outside the core draws nothing and emits console.error in development.

item.media-src.constraint: The address of the photo of the avatar start, or of the picture of the image start. Ignored with another start, and warned once in development. The avatar with no photo shows the person icon; the picture is cropped 1:1 and should be exported at 2x.

item.start-label.constraint: The hidden text of a status start, already localized, such as Complete or Needs attention. It is read only when the item has no end status: with the end status the start icon is decoration. A status start with neither says nothing to a screen reader, and is warned once in development.

item.tag.constraint: A short highlight next to the title, such as New or PRO, already localized. It is an nph-badge primary light, and part of the accessible name.

item.status.constraint: The end status, an nph-badge light of the tone of the status; pending is secondary. Always with text: it needs status-label. A value outside the list draws nothing and emits console.error in development.

item.status-label.constraint: The text of the end status, already localized. A status without it is not drawn, and is warned once in development.

item.indicator.constraint: The Figma property `indicador`. end puts chevron-down after the status and it turns 180 degrees on open. start puts chevron-right before everything, it turns 90 degrees to point down, and the open content lines up with the part after it. A value outside the list draws nothing and emits console.error in development.

item.open.constraint: The Figma property `aberto`, and the current state, as in the native details element. The item starts closed. The person changes it and nph-toggle says so; setting it from code changes the content and fires nothing. An item that is open from the first render does not animate.

item.disabled.constraint: The whole item is faded and the button is disabled: it leaves the Tab order and does not open. With open it is a whole locked section: the content stays in view under the same opacity. A disabled closed content is plain hidden, so the search of the page does not open what the person cannot.

item.persistent.constraint: An open item the person cannot close, the APG case: the trigger takes aria-disabled="true" and stays in the Tab order, and the item keeps the plain open look with no opacity. It opens a closed item. It is not the locked section, which uses disabled.

item.slot.constraint: The default slot of the item is the content, free: any piece goes inside it. It starts collapsible/content-padding-top below the trigger, with no indent for the start media. Actions such as Save stay inside it, with nph-button, never in the trigger.

item.size.constraint: Set by the accordion on every item. Do not set it on an item.

item.heading-level.constraint: Set by the accordion on every item. Do not set it on an item.

item.region.constraint: Set by the accordion on every item, as a property only. False drops role="region" from the content, when the multiple expansion holds more than six items. Do not set it on an item.

nph-toggle.constraint: Fired by an item when the person opens or closes it, by click, Enter, Space, the search of the page or a link to an id inside it, with detail { open }, the state the item is in now. It bubbles and is composed, so the accordion and the page hear it. Setting open from code, and the items the single expansion closes, fire nothing.

appearance.choose_when: grouped in the page body; separated when each section is an independent block; flush in a side panel or inside another container.
do_not_combine_with: grouped inside a card or a dialog, because two outlines add up

expansion.choose_when: multiple when the person compares sections; single in a step-by-step.
do_not_combine_with: single with more than one item meant to stay open

size.choose_when: compact in a dense panel with a pointer; default when in doubt; large on a touch screen.

rest.changes_for_user: Open and closed are told apart by the direction of the indicator and by the content in view, not by color. The open item does not change its background.

hover.changes_for_user: The trigger takes a pill with collapsible/trigger-radius, inset by the container padding in grouped and separated and full width in flush. Hover does not move the focus. An item that cannot change takes no hover.

focus.token: collapsible/focus-border, collapsible/focus-border-width, collapsible/focus-border-radius, collapsible/focus-halo, collapsible/focus-halo-width, collapsible/focus-halo-radius
focus.changes_for_user: For keyboard users, a border and a halo on the trigger, never on the container. The halo may cover the neighbor divider by 1 px; the border stays whole.

disabled.changes_for_user: The whole item is faded, does not open and leaves the Tab order. With open it is a locked section: the content and the status stay in view, faded. The divider and the block outline are the accordion and stay at full.

open_that_does_not_close.changes_for_user: The plain open look with no opacity. The trigger stays in the Tab order and says aria-disabled, and Enter, Space and click do nothing.

business_rules: The accordion keeps what few people read together. Each item starts closed; the page sets open on the ones that are the point of the screen.
Open, the content pushes down what comes below and covers nothing. It closes on no outside click and on no Escape, and the focus stays on the trigger.
The divider is between two items, never before the first or after the last, in grouped and flush. In separated there is no divider and the blocks are accordion/item-gap apart.

Single expansion, more than one item open when it starts, or when it changes from multiple to single: the first item that cannot be closed by the person stays open, else the first in the document, and the others close, with a development warning.

Single expansion, an item marked persistent when another opens: it closes and the mark moves to the item that opened, because the APG keeps one panel open and puts aria-disabled on its button. This follows from the APG, it is not its text.
Single expansion, a locked section (open and disabled): the person did not open it and cannot close it, so the rule leaves it as it is and it does not count as the open item.
With the multiple expansion and more than six items, the content of every item drops role=region, because that many landmarks crowd the page.
One start type per list: the icon (16) and the tile, avatar or image (24 to 48) break the alignment of the titles. The four status icons count as one type.
Show a pending item in text, in the description or in the end status. Never hide an error, a warning or a pending required field in a closed item.
The accordion has no width of its own: it takes the width of its container. 560 is only the reading width of the Figma examples.
Every text comes from the consumer, already localized: the piece writes no word of its own.
domain_errors: An appearance, expansion, size, heading-level, start, status or indicator outside its list, or an icon that is not a core name of nph-icon: the piece draws nothing and emits console.error in development, one per cause.

An icon with a start that is not icon or tile, a media-src with a start that is not avatar or image, a status with no status-label, a status start with no end status and no start-label, more than one item open in the single expansion, and anything but an nph-accordion-item inside the accordion: the piece emits console.warn in development, one per cause.

ai_hints: Use nph-accordion for several supporting sections the person reads one or a few at a time; for a single section use nph-collapsible, and for sections of the same weight seen one at a time use nph-tabs.
Pick the appearance by the place on the screen: grouped in the page body, separated for independent blocks, flush in a side panel or inside another container.
Pick the expansion by the task: multiple to compare, single for a step-by-step.
Match the size to the other controls of the screen: large on a touch screen, compact in a dense panel with a pointer. Set it on the accordion, never on an item.
Write short titles that differ from each other, because people find the section without opening all of them.
Show a pending item in text: in the description, such as 2 fields left, or in the end status, such as Pending. Do not rely on color.
Use one start type in a list: the icon or tile for a topic, the avatar for a person, the image for a product, the status icons for progress.
Put the action, such as Save, inside the content with nph-button, never in the trigger.
Set the heading-level from the page: the accordion is inside a section whose heading is the level above.
Listen to nph-toggle to know what the person did; setting open from code fires nothing.
Do not nest an accordion inside another one.

accessibility.semantics: The accordion pattern of the WAI-ARIA APG, revised without arrows, Home or End. Each trigger is a button with aria-expanded and aria-controls, the only child of a heading whose level comes from the page. The content is a region labelled by the trigger, except in the multiple expansion with more than six items. The indicator and the start media are hidden from assistive technology.
accessibility.accessible_name: The text inside the button, in the order of the parts: title, tag, short description, status. There is no aria-label on the button, which would hide that text. The long description goes in the content. A status start with no end status carries a hidden text, last in the name.
keyboard: Tab and Shift+Tab go through the triggers in page order and through the focusable elements of the open content.
Enter and Space open a closed item and close an open one; the focus stays on the trigger.
Arrows, Home, End and Escape do nothing, and a click outside does not close anything: the content is part of the page.
A disabled item leaves the Tab order. An open item that does not close stays in it.
accessibility.focus: Keyboard only, on the trigger: a border of collapsible/focus-border-width in collapsible/focus-border and a halo outside it. The focus is on the trigger, not on the container. Closing from the page with the focus inside the content moves it to the trigger.
accessibility.contrast: The title meets 4.5:1 on accordion/background and on the hover, in both themes. The description, the indicator and the start icon meet 4.5:1 and 3:1. The status icons meet 3:1. The tile icon meets 4.5:1 in light and the box is decoration in dark. The focus border meets 3:1 on the background and on the hover, in both themes; the known limit against the halo is the one of focus/border. The outline and the divider are decoration.
accessibility.color_alternative: Open and closed are told apart by the direction of the indicator and by the content in view. A status is always text, in the end status or in the description; the start status icon only reinforces it.

invalid_combinations: An appearance, expansion, size, heading-level, start, status or indicator outside its list — the piece draws nothing.
A status with no status-label — the status is not drawn.
An icon that is not a core name of nph-icon — the item draws nothing.
A size set on an item — the accordion overwrites it.
More than one start type in the same list.
An action, a link or a menu inside the trigger.
An error, a warning or a pending required field hidden in a closed item.

parents: a page section, a side panel, a card, a dialog or a step-by-step
children: any piece in the content slot of an item

anti_patterns: Repeating the same title in several sections.
Hiding an error, a warning or a pending required field in a closed item.
Putting a strong outline on each item: use the grouped appearance, with a soft outline on one container, or the separated one.
Using the compact size on a touch screen.
Mixing start types in one list.
Putting an action or a link in the trigger.
Using the grouped appearance inside a card or a dialog.
